name: folio-recursive-pdf-object-validation
instr:
Add opt-in, recursive validation for any PDF object graph, producing deterministic, located, classified diagnostics before unsafe processing begins. Direct validation, reading, decryption, object-stream packing, and output must apply the same rules. Valid or disabled validation must preserve existing behavior and bytes.

In `github.com/carlos7ags/folio/core`, `ValidateObject(object, options)` and `ValidatableObject.ValidatePDF(options)` validate arrays, dictionaries, names, numbers, strings, indirect references, and streams completely, deterministically, without mutation or panic, including cycles and unsupported caller-defined objects. The concrete entry points are `(a *PdfArray) ValidatePDF(options)`, `(d *PdfDictionary) ValidatePDF(options)`, `(n *PdfName) ValidatePDF(options)`, `(n *PdfNumber) ValidatePDF(options)`, `(s *PdfString) ValidatePDF(options)`, `(r *PdfIndirectReference) ValidatePDF(options)`, and `(s *PdfStream) ValidatePDF(options)`. Stream validation treats dictionary metadata and payload as one mutation-free object graph, locating filter defects without compressing data or changing the dictionary. Paths preserve array indexes, dictionary keys and insertion order, stream metadata keys, and both indirect-reference numbers; scalar rules accept every representation already serialized legally.
